newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: LITHUANIA-OPINIONS DIFFER ON REFINERY STAKE-REPORT.
newsitem.headline: LITHUANIA-OPINIONS DIFFER ON REFINERY STAKE-REPORT.

text.p: The opinions of the government and Mazheikiu Nafta oil refinery officials on the state-run stake in the company differ considerably, Lietuvos Rytas newspaper reported on Friday.

The newspaper quoted Economy Minister Vincas Babilius as saying that the state should retain a 34 percent stake in the firm, which is targeting a 20 million litas profit for 1997 after suffering losses for the last five years.
But the chairman of the privatisation commission, Eduardas Vilkas, told the newspaper that 100 percent of the company should be privatised.
"Why should the state control that 34 percent? Probably for the holy peace. Sooner or later all the firm will be sold. It is only the matter of time," Vilkas told the newpaper.
However, the newspaer said that the director general of Mazheikiu Nafta, Gediminas Kiesus, would like the state to maintain 51 percent of the company.
The government approved on Wednesady a decision to include the refinery into the list of companies to be privatised in international tender in 1997-1998.
The share capital of Mazheikiu Nafta is 580 milion litas and 90 percent of it is state-owned.
